title: plugin-auth: an MCP token minted in the same second after a password change is refused 401 (iat in whole seconds vs credential updated_at in ms) since #35822
body:
repo:cloud#5 · hotlong · session_01Q4EjjPP1zuWBNq3nBXVei9

**Defect.** Since PR #35822 (`75925e1c234`, "a password reset ends what the account added before it"), `mcpConsentAdmits` refuses an MCP OAuth access token issued AFTER a password change whenever it falls in the same wall-clock second. The MCP door then answers `401 UNAUTHENTICATED` ("a valid OAuth access token or API key is required") where it should serve the request.

**Cause, read on `origin/main`:**
- `packages/plugins/plugin-auth/src/mcp-token-revocation.ts`, around line 275, calls `issuedBeforeCredentialChange(issuedAt * 1000, readCredentialChangedAt(...))`.
- `issuedAt` is the JWT `iat`, which is in whole seconds. The credential's `updatedAt` is in milliseconds.
- So a token minted at 12:00:00.900, after a change at 12:00:00.400, compares 12:00:00.000 < 12:00:00.400 and is judged "issued before the change".
- `credential-change-ends-prior-access.ts`, around line 173, is a strict `<` on the two values.
- The module's own rule is that access issued after the change is untouched. It carves out a same-second refusal only for `/verify-email` tokens.

**Measured on cloud.** In cloud pin round cloud#4920 (draft PR cloud#4921, pin `493ad095d40e`), `apps/objectos-ee/test/scim-leaver-lifecycle.e2e.test.ts` fails its PREMISE. The test changes a password, then grants an MCP agent through DCR + PKCE + authorize/consent/token/refresh and calls `tools/list`. The call answers 401, deterministically when the file runs alone. A diagnostic 1100 ms pause after the change, since reverted, turns the file 42/42 green. The same test passed at pin `dea68e93c68d`, which predates #35822.

**Reach.** Any scripted or agent flow that connects over MCP right after a password change or reset, on any deployment. The behaviour fails closed: it refuses a valid token and never admits an old one. It is not a security finding.

**Fix shape: a security-boundary choice the platform lane must make.** One rule must stay true: a token issued before the change is never admitted. Options:
- (a) carry a sub-second issue time for MCP tokens and compare it in ms;
- (b) compare at second resolution and treat the change second as "after" only for tokens provably minted after it;
- (c) rule the same-second refusal deliberate, as for `/verify-email`, and document it in the module, so that clients retry after one second.

Whichever is chosen needs a test pinning it: a token minted after the change in the same second, and a token minted before the change in the same second.

**Why it matters to cloud.** Cloud's pin round cloud#4920 cannot land past `75925e1c234` while this test is red. #35822 is an ancestor of the #35939 fix that the round needs, so the round cannot pin around it. Cloud#4920 blocks cloud#4918 (p1). Under the standing rule 「平台问题在平台修」, cloud does not add a wait to its security-list test unless the platform rules (c).

Re-check: `git grep -n "issuedBeforeCredentialChange(issuedAt \* 1000" -- packages/plugins/plugin-auth/src/mcp-token-revocation.ts` still hits ⇒ the defect is present.
